note: Introductions and plantings from the USGS Nonindigenous Aquatic Species database plus documented early events. Native fish stocked in their native range, such as Lahontan cutthroat trout plants, are not in these records; NDOW stocking reports on the Stocking tab cover recent years.

statewide.text: Common Carp: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
The first fish are carried into Nevada by rail: eastern brook trout and other species released into streams near the Central Pacific line.
Lahontan cutthroat trout: first Nevada record, Kingston Creek, south of Austin of the east side of the Toiyabe Range.
Bonneville cutthroat trout: first Nevada record, Moorman Ranch {near} (Illipah) in Jakes Valley.
Nevada creates its first Fish Commission to restock waters emptied by mining, logging and irrigation diversions.
Sacramento Perch: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
White Catfish: first Nevada record, Washoe Lake.
Lake Whitefish: first Nevada record, Lake Tahoe.
Brown Bullhead: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Chinook Salmon: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
coastal rainbow trout: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Brook Trout: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Atlantic Salmon: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Tench: first Nevada record, Virginia City.
Smallmouth Bass: first Nevada record, Carson River.
Lake Trout: first Nevada record, Lake Tahoe.
Rainbow Trout: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Goldfish: first Nevada record, Blue Eagle Ranch, east of Railroad Valley.
Brown Trout: first Nevada record, Truckee River.
Largemouth Bass: first Nevada record, Reno and vicinity.
Bluegill: first Nevada record, Olsen's Lake at Ely.
Black Bullhead: first Nevada record, Lake, SE Nevada, W of Fort Mohave, Arizona.
Golden Trout: first Nevada record, Lake Tahoe.
Black Crappie: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Westslope Cutthroat Trout: first Nevada record, Walker Lake drainage.
Yellow Perch: first Nevada record, West Carson River near Genoa.
Western Mosquitofish: first Nevada record, Fallon [unspecified waters].
Sockeye Salmon: first Nevada record, lake, reservoirs and streams of west-central Nevada.
Channel Catfish: first Nevada record, Washoe Lake.

Lahontan cutthroat trout of Pyramid Lake, the largest cutthroat trout ever recorded, die out there after Derby Dam (1905) cuts off the Truckee River spawning run. Hatchery plants of other strains keep the lake fished until the original strain is rediscovered in Utah and returned in the 2000s.
Mountain Sucker: first Nevada record, Lake Mead.
Green Sunfish: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Chum Salmon: first Nevada record, Lahontan Reservoir (probably) Churchill County.
Amargosa pupfish: first Nevada record, Pahrump Ranch in Pahrump Valley.
Amargosa Pupfish: first Nevada record, spring on the Las Vegas golf course.
Arctic Grayling: first Nevada record, Ruby Valley.
Tui Chub: first Nevada record, Stone Cabin (=Willow Creek) Valley.
American Shad: first Nevada record, Colorado River.
Yellowstone cutthroat trout: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
greenback cutthroat trout: first Nevada record, Humboldt River near Elko.
Utah Chub: first Nevada record, Shoshone Ponds, near Ely, Spring Valley.
Railroad Valley Springfish: first Nevada record, artificial ponds at Sodaville, southeastern part of Mineral County, west side of highway 95.
Virgin Spinedace: first Nevada record, Lake Mead Boat Dock.
Sacramento Blackfish: first Nevada record, state non-specific.
Golden Shiner: first Nevada record, Colorado River.
Lahontan speckled dace: first Nevada record, Ruby Marsh.
Threadfin Shad: first Nevada record, Overton Arm of Lake Mead.
White Crappie: first Nevada record, Rye Patch Reservoir, on the Humboldt River.
black bass: first Nevada record, Adams-McGill Reservoir, Sunnyside Wildlife Management Area in extreme NE Nye County on the White River.
Lahontan Redside: first Nevada record, Railroad Valley Pond No. 2.
Kamloops trout: first Nevada record, Pyramid Lake and above in the Truckee River.
Speckled Dace: first Nevada record, Rogers Spring (Overton Arm of Lake Mead).
Striped bass are first planted in Lake Mead; they become the lake's main sport fish.
